title: Flex cushion + exchange-rate headcount sensitivity Q2 2026
summary: Working workbook to quantify headcount / burn tradeoffs versus pricing changes and FX swings for the spring Q2 planning window. Tests 3 flex-cushion models (reserve pool, soft-commit, credit-line) across a set of token-demand shocks and USD:EUR exchange-rate movements to produce recommended hiring gates.
body:
Purpose:
- Short, practical finance workbook to be used in weekly capacity syncs for the next 12 weeks. Focus: how much headcount (FTEs / contractors) can be added or deferred under different price elasticity + exchange-rate scenarios while keeping runway >= 10 months.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Starting runway (USD): $48,500,000 as of 2026-04-01
- Monthly gross burn (people + infra): $3,800,000 baseline
- Token rate mix (hosted API): 70% text-gen, 20% embeddings, 10% other
- Average price per 1k tokens (baseline): $0.035
- FX exposure: 22% of vendor costs are EUR-denominated; base USD:EUR = 1.09 on 2026-04-01
- Hiring lead time: 6 weeks to full productivity (ic or infra ramp)
- Contractor delta: +30% cost per FTE equivalent but 0.6x ramp lead time

Combined scenarios (pricing + FX): we project 9 model permutations (3 pricing x 3 FX) and run headcount gate calculation.

Headcount gate logic (rules-of-thumb captured here):
- Gate Green: Add up to 8 FTEs over 12 weeks if runway stays >= 11 months and burn increase <= 8% and net margin per route improves.
- Gate Yellow: Add up to 4 FTEs or prefer contractors if runway between 9–11 months or burn increase between 8–14%.
- Gate Red: Pause hiring / convert to contractor if runway < 9 months or burn increase > 14% (trigger immediate exec review).

Sample outputs from the model (snapshots):
- Scenario A (price cut -10%, FX base): Runway improves marginally (+0.7 months) due to demand uplift; Gate = Green; recommended hires = 6 FTEs (mix 4 eng / 1 infra / 1 sales ops).
- Scenario B (price raise +5%, FX +10% vendor cost): Runway shortens by 0.9 months; Gate = Yellow; recommended hires = 2 contractors (3-month term) for product infra tasks.
- Scenario C (competitor price shock -20%, FX -10%): Demand shift unpredictable; net revenue down 9% but volume up; Gate = Yellow->Red threshold; recommend hiring freeze and prioritize on-call infra shifts.

Sensitivity formulas (for sheet):
- Projected revenue = baseline_revenue * (1 + price_change) * (1 + elasticity * price_change_sign)
- Adjusted infra cost = baseline_infra * (1 + EUR_share * FX_move)
- New monthly burn = baseline_burn + incremental_people_cost + (adjusted_infra - baseline_infra)
- Runway months = cash_balance / monthly_burn

Action items and playbook (short):
- Finance: finalize monthly true-up cadence; implement scenario A/B/C dashboards in Looker (owner: Aaron Li) by 2026-04-23.
- Recruiting: pre-approve interview loops for the 6 headcount bundle in scenario A; hold contractor bench list (Priya Desai) for yellow gate.
- Product / Sales: flag top-10 customers for potential churn under price raise; prepare targeted comms for price cut landing page.
- Ops: run stress tests on Dedicated pools for +15% traffic and ensure autoscale triggers in private deployments (Connor Blake).

Open questions / to validate:
- Real elasticity by customer segment (enterprise vs PLG) — we need historical A/B data (ask growth analytics).
- Exact share of EUR-denominated vendor spend (contract team reviewing).
- Contractor cost uplift assumptions vs. actual quotes for specialized infra contractors.

Notes to self (rough):
- This workbook intentionally over-indexes on short window (12w) because hiring lead times compress decisions.
- Keep the reserve pool (flex cushion) at 8–12% of monthly burn to cover quantization adoption / infra price variance.
- Consider small, targeted price experiments (2–4% bandwidth) before broad raises to measure elasticity per token-route.

Appendix (quick numbers used in modeling):
- Baseline monthly revenue (Apr 2026): $5,200,000
- Baseline monthly infra: $1,080,000
- Baseline people cost (monthly): $2,400,000
- Cash balance (Apr 2026): $48,500,000
- FTE blended fully-loaded cost (annual): $210,000 => monthly ~17,500
- Contractor FTE-eq monthly: ~$22,750

If this draft looks ok, I'll convert to a proper multi-tab sheet with scenario dashboards and a pivot for per-route margin and pass to looker team for dashboarding.
